name: O'NEILL, Deborah (Deb) Mary

headline.note: Official and first-person biographical sources establish secondary-school teaching followed by University of Newcastle lecturing, while a 2013 interview identifies St Edward's as O'Neill's first full-time teaching job, later teaching at Corpus Christi, part-time university lecturing and a family lawn-mowing business. The Catholic-school roles are nonprofit and university employment is separated under the codebook; the business lacks dates, hours and evidence of substantive full-time work. Exact teaching and university boundaries, leave and overlaps remain unknown, so neither public nor private full-time years can be calculated.

career_spells.employer: Parents' construction and plant-hire business (unidentified entity)
career_spells.role: Assisted with invoicing as a child
career_spells.evidence_note: Biographical accounts say O'Neill took responsibility for invoicing in her parents' construction and plant-hire business from about age 11. The entity, exact dates, pay, hours and legal employment status are not identified.
career_spells.counting_note: Childhood family assistance is not treated as documented adult paid employment.

career_spells.employer: University of Sydney; University of New England; Australian Catholic University; Deakin University
career_spells.role: BA, Diploma of Teaching, MA and Graduate Diploma in Literacy Education student
career_spells.evidence_note: The official biography lists four qualifications. O'Neill's 2013 interview describes interruption of her initial arts degree, later teacher training and a master's undertaken while teaching and raising children. Enrolment, completion dates, study loads and employment overlaps are unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: Study is excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.evidence_note: In the Sisters of the Good Samaritan interview O'Neill says she was a student teacher at Mercy College, where she met her future husband. The source does not establish paid employment, dates, hours or placement conditions.
career_spells.counting_note: A student-teaching placement is treated as study unless paid employment is established.

career_spells.evidence_note: O'Neill's 2013 interview identifies St Edward's as her first full-time job after moving to the Central Coast. The official biography confirms a high-school teaching career, but exact appointment/cessation dates, subjects, leave and the employer entity are unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: The source directly supports full-time status, but employment by a nongovernment Catholic school is classified nonprofit and excluded from the narrow public/private headline.

career_spells.evidence_note: The 2013 interview says O'Neill later taught at Corpus Christi College, during a period in which her three children were born. Exact appointment dates, subjects, hours, leave, career breaks and transition from St Edward's are unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: Nongovernment Catholic-school employment is classified nonprofit and excluded from the narrow headline; full-time status is not assumed from the teacher title.

career_spells.employer: University of Newcastle, School of Education, Central Coast Campus
career_spells.evidence_note: Official and party biographies identify the University of Newcastle role before Parliament; O'Neill's 2013 interview explicitly calls the lecturing part-time and says it occurred while she was teaching and raising children. ABC described her as a university academic at the March 2010 preselection and as a local lecturer in its 2013 election guide. Start date, FTE fraction, leave, exact cessation and overlap with school teaching and campaigning are unresolved; the federal election date is only an upper bound for the pre-parliamentary description.
career_spells.counting_note: University employment is separately classified and excluded under the current codebook; part-time work without a defensible FTE fraction would not support a full-time duration in any event.

career_spells.evidence_note: O'Neill's 2013 interview says she and her husband established a lawn-mowing business while she was teaching, studying and raising children. The legal entity, ownership split, dates, duties, customers, revenue or remuneration, hours, leave and continuation are unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: Self-employment may count only when substantive full-time work and boundaries are supported; co-founding or ownership alone is insufficient.

career_spells.role: State Conference delegate and other party offices
career_spells.evidence_note: The current parliamentary biography records State Conference delegate service from 1996 and national-conference delegations in 2007 and 2009, plus undated junior vice-president and national-policy roles. Secondary synthesis reports NSW party vice-presidency from December 2011 to 2024. Remuneration, workload and exact boundaries for each office are unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: Party organisational activity is excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.role: Candidate for Gosford at the NSW election
career_spells.evidence_note: ABC's 2013 Robertson guide and secondary chronology identify the unsuccessful 2003 candidacy. Nomination and election dates, remuneration, hours and overlap with teaching, lecturing and the family business are unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: Party candidacy and campaigning are excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.role: Candidate for Terrigal at the NSW election
career_spells.evidence_note: ABC's 2013 Robertson guide and secondary chronology identify the unsuccessful 2007 candidacy. Nomination and election dates, remuneration, hours and overlap with employment are unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: Party candidacy and campaigning are excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.evidence_note: ABC reported O'Neill winning Labor preselection on 6 March 2010; the parliamentary biography records election on 21 August 2010. Campaign remuneration, hours and overlap with university or other employment are unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: Party candidacy and campaigning are excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.role: Member of the House of Representatives for Robertson
career_spells.evidence_note: Official parliamentary service history records election in 2010 and defeat at the 7 September 2013 general election.
career_spells.counting_note: Federal elected office is excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.role: Employment status between House defeat and Senate appointment unresolved
career_spells.evidence_note: Official service history establishes a gap after House defeat and before the NSW Parliament selected O'Neill for the Senate vacancy. Reviewed sources do not identify paid employment in this interval; absence of evidence is not coded as unemployment.
career_spells.counting_note: No sector or duration is inferred for an unresolved interval.

career_spells.role: Senator for New South Wales (casual-vacancy appointment)
career_spells.evidence_note: The official parliamentary biography records selection by the NSW Parliament on 13 November 2013 to replace Bob Carr and service through 30 June 2014.
career_spells.counting_note: Federal elected office is excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.evidence_note: The parliamentary biography records a renewed NSW parliamentary choice on 2 July 2014, election to the Senate in 2016 and re-election in 2022; service was current at the frozen snapshot.
career_spells.counting_note: Federal elected office is excluded under the codebook.

research_notes: Blocked pending exact dates, subjects, hours, leave and career breaks for St Edward's and Corpus Christi teaching, including whether any other school employers are omitted.
Resolve Mercy student-teaching conditions and all degree enrolment/completion dates so study, teaching, maternity or other leave and university work can be aligned without inventing continuity.
Obtain University of Newcastle appointment records, title progression, campus/school, start and cessation dates, FTE fraction, leave and overlap with teaching, study, business and campaigns.
Identify the lawn-mowing business entity, dates, ownership, duties, customers, remuneration, hours, leave and whether it continued through candidacies or federal service.
Determine remuneration and workload for ALP offices and the 2003, 2007 and 2010 campaigns; identify any paid work in the September–November 2013 parliamentary gap.

No public/private full-time duration is inferred from the generic teacher/lecturer labels. The directly described full-time St Edward's role remains a nonprofit exclusion; missing evidence is not zero.
